subject: Capacity harmonization and mid-term add — quote request
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nimbushealth.com>
To: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity harmonization and mid-term add — quick context

Hi Karthik,

Quick context from my side — we run two Dedicated GPU pools with Redwood (AlphaPool: 48 A100s / BetaPool: 12 A100s) under the existing contract (PO attached in our system). Our Q1 telemetry shows AlphaPool peaking at 92% utilization during model training windows and BetaPool sitting idle ~40% of the day. We expect a product push in July that will shift steady-state inference traffic across both pools.

Goals:
- Add capacity ahead of July launch without breaking our commit economics
- Harmonize pool sizing so we can autoscale predictably across workloads
- Lock a throughput SLA for customer-facing inference paths (p50 latency target and sustained tokens/sec guarantees)

Ask: can Redwood provide a proposal that preserves our current committed rate card for existing commit, gives a price break on incremental GPUs, and includes a short-term top-up option that converts into committed capacity by renewal? Ideally we want clear pricing for: (a) one-off top-up (30 days), (b) 3-month staged add, (c) immediate commit conversion with discount tiers. Also need the timeline for procurement/DocuSign.

I attached a small usage extract (current_usage_report_q1_2027.csv).

Thanks — Sara
Sara Bennett
Head of Platform Operations, Nimbus Health
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity harmonization and mid-term add — quick context

Sara — thanks for the context and the usage extract, that helps a lot. Quick summary of practical options; I copied Marissa (Sales Ops) and Jonas (Solutions) to align on SLA/throughput sizing and on final quote shape.

1) Short-term top-up (30 days)
   - We provision additional 16 A100-equivalent nodes into AlphaPool as a burst/top-up.
   - Rate: billed at our on-demand Dedicated top-up rate (no long-term discount), refundable as a credit if converted to commit within 60 days.
   - Good when you need capacity immediately for a short runway.

2) Staged add (3-month ramp)
   - 3-month staged deployment: +8 nodes month 1, +8 nodes month 2, + -- final 8 month 3 (example split).
   - We can front-load a partial discount (7%) on incremental nodes for staged commitments if you sign an addendum.

3) Immediate commit conversion (preferred economics)
   - Convert incremental capacity into a reserved commit for the remainder of your contract term.
   - Pricing tiers: +8 GPUs -> 6% discount on incremental units; +16 GPUs -> 9% discount; +32 GPUs -> 12% discount.
   - Throughput guarantees: we can add a per-route throughput SLA (tokens/sec) for production endpoints behind a minimal SLO acceptance test and a small latency guardband. SLA credits are limited to a % of monthly invoice on verified misses.

Attachments: I drafted a short capacity-harmonization-plan.xlsx (attached) that lays out options with simple math against your Q1 usage.

Questions for you:
- Which of the three options looks closest to your preferred procurement path?
- Do you need a formal PO amendment or will a signed DocuSign addendum suffice?
- Any regulatory constraints (e.g., must be in a specific cloud region) that affect where we place the extra GPUs?

I[0m
Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nimbushealth.com>
To: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity harmonization and mid-term add — quick context

Karthik — thanks, that breakdown is super helpful. Were leaning to option 3 (immediate commit conversion) to get the unit economics and predictable run rate. A couple clarifications before I send this to procurement:
- Can you confirm the 9% incremental tier for +16 GPUs is off the current committed rate (not the on-demand top-up rate)?
- If we convert on Day 1 of deployment, can our on-demand spend against that incremental capacity be credited and applied to the first invoice?
- Timeline: can you provide a formal quote/addendum and DocuSign by EOD Friday so procurement can review next week?

If you can confirm the crediting behavior and get the addendum out by Friday, Ill route to PO approval.

— Sara
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity harmonization and mid-term add — quick context

Sara — confirmed on both counts: the 9% is applied to incremental units off your existing committed rate card (not the on-demand top-up). If you convert within the first billing period, the on-demand top-up charges are applied as a credit toward the first committed invoice (we've built that into the addendum).

Marissa and Vanessa have prepared a formal quote and a DocuSign addendum (attached: NIM-2027-07-formal-quote.pdf). Key next steps:
- Sara: approve the quote and confirm preferred start date (we recommend 2027-05-03 to allow provisioning and acceptance tests).
- Marissa: issue DocuSign and set procurement contact for PO cross-reference.
- Jonas: run the SLA acceptance test plan against your staging endpoints during the first 72 hours of provisioning.

I'll open a small internal work item to track the conversion and credits; will update the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign link.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: NIM-2027-07-formal-quote.pdf
